messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: runtime-high-95th-latency fired for service=inference-gateway environment=prod (alert_id: pgd-9921)
pagerduty: Triggered on escalation policy: oncall-sre-primary. Notified alex.s.
alex.s: acked. I’m looking at traces/metrics now. seeing brief spike in 95th token latency from 11:02:10 to 11:04:05 UTC.
mira_k: on it too — checking autoscaler logs and queue length. Could be short GC/worker churn.
danb: running quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` --> a couple pods restarted ~11:02. Logs show OOM kill on runtime-worker-7.
alex.s: paste of logs: ```[11:01:58] runtime-worker-7 OOMKilled pid=2145 rss=3.9G
[11:02:02] runtime-worker-7 restarted successfully
[11:03:50] request queue depth spike to 420 (baseline 80)```
mira_k: thanks. Autoscaler kicked in, new pods came up but initial backlog caused token latencies to spike. Not a model degradation.
incident-bot: PagerDuty state changed: alert auto-resolved (duration ~2m).
pagerduty: Auto-resolved by monitoring. No ack escalation required.
alex.s: confirmed from traces — end-to-end request p95 dropped back to normal by 11:05. Looks like short resource pressure then recovered.
danb: quick mitigation notes: lower burst window for client-side retries? or add prefix caching for short queries. But immediate thing: adjust HPA target to be slightly higher during peak windows.
mira_k: +1. Also propose we suppress repeat flapping alerts: add 3m evaluation window for p95 and require >2m sustained over threshold before page.
alex.s: agree on alert debounce. For now I'll silence pgd-9921 for 30m while we monitor. Doing mute now.
alex.s: `/pagerduty mute pgd-9921 30m` (command issued)
incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty incident muted for 30m by alex.s.
sre-handoff-bot: heads-up: on-call handoff in 20m; @mira_k will be primary after 11:30 UTC.
mira_k: thanks — I’ll take primary and keep an eye on the autoscaler and OOM patterns.
danb: quick checklist item: add memory headroom to runtime-worker image or set memoryRequests higher. I’ll open a short-lived PR with config bump.
alex.s: customer impact check: looked at customer-facing error rates — 5xx did not increase beyond noise, no customer tickets so far. Marking impact = minimal/transient.
mira_k: filing a follow-up ticket with triage notes and suggested alert tuning: INF-2745.
alex.s: assign INF-2745 to danb for config change, mira_k for alert debounce and follow-up monitoring.
incident-bot: Thread closed (auto-resolved alert).
alex.s: final note — this looks like a flapping transient caused by a memory pressure + request burst. No rollback required. Keep mute until we validate HPA changes in staging. We'll revisit if repeats in next 24h. :thumbsup:
mira_k: adding evaluation dashboard panel for burst-to-capacity ratio.
danb: PR opened: runtime: bump memoryRequest from 3Gi to 4Gi on worker pod (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1421).
alex.s: thanks team. If it flaps again, escalate to infra-eng for capacity planning, otherwise closing thread. :white_check_mark:
